title: The p-value: what it says and what it does not

videos.script: Lesson thirteen ended with a decision. Reject the null, or do not. This lesson adds the number that most reports print beside that decision: the p-value. {{decision}} For Horta's routing test, the p-value is about point one six. For the filling machine, it is less than one in a thousand. {{values}} Here is what it means. Imagine the null hypothesis is true. The routing changed nothing. How often would a sample of twenty-five deliveries look at least as favourable to the supplier as this one did? About one time in six. {{means}} That is all a p-value is. A measure of how surprising the data would be, if nothing were going on. {{all}} It is not the chance that the null is true. It is not the chance that the result is a fluke. It does not say how big the effect is. People misread it in all three ways, including people who publish research. {{misread}} And it has a weakness that has caused real damage. Run enough tests on nothing, and some will come out small by chance. You will watch it happen to twenty tests at once. {{damage}}
